Source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record - Cholera in Africa (WER 1991;66(42), 18 October 1991)
Description: WHO review of cholera in Africa 1970-1991 (data as at 19 September 1991), published at the height of the 1991 African epidemic wave. CONTAINS THE DECISIVE STATEMENT FOR BENIN'S 1987-1990 ABSENCE, verbatim: 'Countries which had not reported cholera for several years (Benin, Burkina Faso, Chad, Togo) have reported cases in 1991 (Map 2).' French: 'Des pays ont notifie des cas en 1991 (Carte 2), qui ne rapportaient plus de cholera depuis plusieurs annees (Benin, Burkina Faso, Tchad, Togo).' This is WHO NAMING Benin as a country that had not reported cholera for several years before 1991 - a positive statement of prior absence, not an inference from table omission. It matches the WER annual tables and the WHO GHO series exactly: Benin's last notification before 1991 was 243 cases in 1986, i.e. four consecutive silent years 1987-1990. The article also recaps the 1970-71 introduction: 'From Conakry, the disease first surged out eastwards along the coast, reaching Sierra Leone, Liberia, Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana, Togo, Dahomey (now Benin), Nigeria and southern Cameroon successively between September 1970 and February 1971.'
